engagement_title: Aldervale Mutual producer kit: rebuild the counter card run from the file that went to press, bring fourteen self-submitted producer headshots to one house look, and hand back the advisor deck, the plan one-pager and the premium infographic as documents the compliance desk can edit itself
vertical: Finance and insurance, a ninety-one-year-old policyholder-owned mutual life insurer selling whole life and final expense through appointed producers across New England
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring Upwork insurance-agency posting in which an agency marketing manager asks a freelancer to 'redesign our agent one-pager and build a slide deck our producers can actually present at the kitchen table', supplying a roster spreadsheet, a folder of agent headshots 'of wildly varying quality, everyone sent us whatever they had', and a PDF of the current printed card, with the standing requirement that everything come back 'editable so we can update rates and the disclosure ourselves without coming back to you'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com variable-data posting from a financial services office needing 'personalised counter cards, one per advisor, print ready, plus an individual PDF for each so we can reprint one at a time', worked from an existing printed card whose original designer is no longer reachable. Both real clients, their carrier and their compliance language are laundered to the fictional Aldervale Mutual. The ledger's STRENGTHEN verdict was correct that the original concept sat almost entirely on the authoring surface: the fuller commission this client genuinely has begins at fourteen phone-camera headshots and a retired printer's press file, runs through a regulated variable-data card run, and only then reaches the deck and the one-pager.
client_one_liner: Our producers sit at kitchen tables, everything we hand them has to survive that, and the printer who built our counter cards has closed, so all we have is the file that went to press.
client_brief:
Aldervale Mutual, producer kit for the 2027 selling season

We are a policyholder-owned mutual, ninety-one years old, and we sell whole life and final expense through appointed producers across New England. Our producers sit at kitchen tables. Everything we give them has to survive that.

Three things need rebuilding before January.

First, the counter cards. Every producer has a card at the branch counter and at the community bank desks we share space in: their name, their license line, their office, their photograph and the disclosure our compliance desk writes. Our old printer built them and she has closed. We have the file that went to press and nothing else. We are doing the Northern district first, fourteen producers. We need the whole run again on the current roster with the current disclosure, a proof per producer that compliance can sign off, and a separate file per producer so we can reprint one without touching the rest.

Second, the headshots. We asked producers to send us a photograph. What came back came back from fourteen different phones in fourteen different offices. They need to look like they work for the same company.

Third, the client-facing pieces: the deck a producer walks a family through, the one page that compares our three plans, and something that shows what a premium actually buys at different ages. All three have to be editable by us, because rates move every year and the disclosure language changes when a state changes it, and I am not paying for a redo each time.

We own no photograph of a family and we may not use a policyholder's. If there is something honest for the deck opener that is not one of our own people, use it.

Finally a short written note for the file: what you did, what type we are on, and anything you had to ask us about.

Our premiums run forty five to a hundred and eighty a month. Our people are thirty five to sixty and they are buying this because they do not want to be a burden. Sober, plain, trustworthy. Nothing that looks like an advertisement.
price_band_and_audience: Whole life and final expense at forty five to a hundred and eighty dollars a month, sold face to face to households aged thirty five to sixty with modest savings, whose stated motive is not wanting to leave a burden. The band is load-bearing in both directions. At this price and this motive the correct grammar is sober and plain: a muted institutional palette, generous white space, a benefit table that reads like a table rather than a graphic, one restrained accent used only to mark the recommended plan, and type that carries authority without announcing itself. Pushed upward into the gold-rule, deep-navy, serif-display register of a private wealth manager it misreads the buyer entirely and reads as a product they cannot afford. Pushed downward into a bright promotional layout with burst callouts and exclamation-weight headlines it reads as a direct-response mailer, which is exactly the register a regulated mutual's compliance desk rejects and exactly the register that makes a thirty five year old distrust a ninety-one year old carrier. A real posted commission of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Owned by the people we cover.
brand_identity.sector: A policyholder owned mutual life insurer selling whole life and final expense through appointed producers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1935, a mutual serving New England, ninety one years old, selling face to face through producers across the region.
brand_identity.about: Aldervale Mutual is owned by its policyholders, not by shareholders. It sells whole life and final expense cover through appointed producers who sit with families at kitchen tables. Its promise is quiet reliability: modest premiums, plain terms and a carrier that has been paying claims for ninety one years.
brand_identity.audience: Households aged 35 to 60 with modest savings, buying because they do not want to leave a burden. They trust plainness and distrust anything that reads like a sales pitch.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premiums run 45 to 180 dollars a month, drop in comparison irrelevant. A regulated mutual at a modest, accessible band, deliberately not a private wealth manager and not a discount direct response mailer.
brand_identity.typography: Type that carries authority without announcing itself. A traditional text serif for body and disclosures, a clean sans for labels and figures, one restrained accent used only to mark the recommended plan. Generous white space, tables that read like tables.
brand_identity.voice: Sober, plain and reassuring, written the way a trusted advisor speaks across a table. No exclamation, no urgency. Example line the brand would write: A whole life policy is a promise that holds its value, and the premium you start with is the premium you keep.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The printer who built the counter cards has closed, so the only counter card artwork that survives is the flat press PDF that went to press. Producer headshots are self submitted from personal phones and vary widely. Compliance owns the disclosure language and updates it when a state changes its rules.
brand_identity.values: Nothing may read as an advertisement, and everything must survive the kitchen table. Compliance and honesty come before flourish, and the material should feel as dependable as the carrier behind it.

assets_supplied.name: producer_headshots/ (14 frames, mixed dimensions, 900 to 4000 px on the long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: Self-submitted producer photographs, one per producer in the Northern district, taken on personal phones in branch offices and at home over about three weeks.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What came back came back from fourteen different phones in fourteen different offices."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Five producers stood against the branch's mid-grey painted wall in a charcoal or navy suit, so the shoulder line and the ground sit at nearly the same luminance and a knockout takes a bite out of the shoulder while reporting success and returning a plausible file. Two frames are small phone captures that cannot fill the card's photograph area at native scale, and one carries a partner bank's counter signage legible behind the producer.

assets_supplied.name: countercard_2026_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's flat press PDF for the counter card, 4 by 6 inches portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the producer name, the license line, the office line, the disclosure paragraph and a placed photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer ran. We only have what went to press and she has closed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The four printed copy blocks do not arrive as four addressable frames and which of them share a story with which is not predictable from the printed card, so some fields must be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside a single flow. The disclosure sits in a fixed-measure frame sized in 2026 to the single sentence compliance used that year, and a frame like that does not spill: it simply stops rendering at its boundary.

assets_supplied.name: producer_roster_northern.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the licensing system, one row per appointed producer in the Northern district, with columns for name, license line, office, state, disclosure text and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The fourteen for the Northern district, straight out of the licensing system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One producer resigned in November and the export still carries her. Two producers are dually licensed in a second state and their disclosure cell holds a materially longer state-specific paragraph than the sentence the other twelve carry. And one row's photo column names a file nobody actually sent.

assets_supplied.name: plan_rates_2027.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The actuarial rate table for the three plans, by issue age band and by coverage amount, as the pricing desk exports it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What a premium buys, by age. This is the file the rate infographic has to be true to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the three plans are quoted as a rate per thousand dollars of coverage while the third is quoted as a flat monthly premium, and no column anywhere says which is which. Laid straight into one table or one chart axis the three plans present three different kinds of number as though they were comparable.

assets_supplied.name: compliance_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the compliance officer on what may and may not appear on client-facing material, and what she means by an advertisement.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What compliance will and will not sign."

acceptance_bar: The fourteen producers read as fourteen people photographed by one company: one skin rendering, one background value, one head size in the frame, one crop logic. A producer whose frame cannot be brought to the set is named to us, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every counter card plate is a clean separation of the producer from the ground, with the shoulder line and the collar intact when the card is viewed at print size rather than at preview scale.
No delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop or resize operation's tradeoff record carries an enlargement entry.
Exactly one counter card per active producer, no extra card and no missing card. If the number shipped is not fourteen the note says which row was left out and why.
Every card carries all four copy blocks the 2026 card carried, and every card's photograph is the producer named on the card.

Every card's disclosure appears in full, as a complete sentence ending where compliance wrote it ending, on the rendered card at true trim. A disclosure that stops short anywhere is a compliance failure regardless of how the card looks otherwise.
Each per-producer file contains the producer its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order files came back in.
The compliance proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The deck, the one-pager and the premium infographic come back as one native editable document we can change a rate in, with every photograph actually visible, the plan comparison as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.

The plan comparison presents the three plans as comparable only where they are comparable, and any footnote that qualifies the whole table sits under the whole table as one readable sentence rather than in fragments.
Nothing in the client-facing set reads as an advertisement under the standard in the compliance note, and nothing reads as private wealth management either.
Anything on the deck opener that is not one of our own people is honest about being that, and it sits with the producer portraits rather than against them.

A written note: what was applied to each portrait and why that portrait differs, the type system by role, every roster row questioned and how it was resolved, what the press file conversion actually exposed, and every enlargement any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_auto_tone, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked), image_select_subject and image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, upscale_factor and detection_confidence)
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole portrait deliverable. It brings fourteen frames shot on fourteen phones under fourteen lighting conditions to one house rendering one call at a time, then produces the counter card plates by separating each producer from whatever office they stood in and setting them on the house neutral. Separation quality here is a property of each individual photograph rather than of the parameters chosen, selections come back fully binary with no intermediate values, and the only enlargement signal anywhere is the tradeoffs array on the crop call.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The counter card run, which is the only genuine record-per-page job in the engagement. The retired printer's press file becomes a live merge template, the licensing export becomes the data source after reconciliation, and the run yields the press cards, the per-producer single files the branch reprints from, and the compliance proofs. The true story text has to be reconstructed from the exported interchange file rather than trusted from the mapping readout, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The advisor deck, the plan one-pager at true physical dimensions, the premium infographic as inline SVG that stays editable vector, and the advisor-brand basis page, all as one native editable document so the marketing desk can change a rate itself. Every photograph inlined as image data, the plan comparison authored as a genuine table, family and weight declared per text element, each root declaring its own canvas, and the payload routed by uploaded URL because a deck's worth of portraits passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the deck, the one-pager, the infographic and the basis page, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, since no font chosen here can reach the printed counter card. The pairing is the agent's own art direction against a regulated mutual at a modest premium band, the numeric weight is non-standard per family, one unlaundered name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug rather than the PostScript name.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the honest deck opener the mutual may lawfully use, IP-clean and at camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded, since a policyholder's photograph is not available to it. The Boards half persists the portrait selects and the opener candidate for the compliance officer's sign off before the card run is committed, placed within the twelve-per-call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: counter cards to the merge surface, deck and one-pager and infographic to authored canvases, portraits to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout the mutual wants preserved; the client-facing pieces are free-form and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the fourteen headshots, the press PDF, the licensing export, the rate table and the compliance note, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by producer and by role, because the same frame will exist in three states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by producer and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen frames and triage: available headroom, background value, head size in frame, colour cast, and how much edge each frame has to spare against the card's photograph area.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen phones produce fourteen different problems, and which producers can reach the card's frame at native scale is a fact about the files rather than a decision.
trajectory.produces: A per-producer triage note: cast, ground, head size, native dimensions and edge margin.

trajectory.action: Fix one house rendering and bring each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: One skin rendering and one background value across fourteen sources means fourteen different routes to one destination rather than one batched move, and the compliance note rules out anything that reads as retouched.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen normalised portraits at source scale with a per-producer parameter log.

trajectory.action: Lay the fourteen normalised portraits together as a branch counter would show them side by side and judge them as one company.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set at the only moment the comparison exists, and deciding whether any producer has been pushed far enough to stop looking like the other thirteen.
trajectory.produces: A set judged as a set, with any portrait that will not join it named.

trajectory.action: Separate each producer from the office they were photographed in and set them on the house neutral to make the fourteen counter card plates.
trajectory.judgement: Whether to knock out to the house ground in one operation or to select, invert and confine the correction is a choice per frame, and the ground each producer happened to stand against is what decides it. Signage in a frame is a matter for the client, not a silent removal.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen counter card plates on the house neutral.

trajectory.action: Derive each plate at the card's photograph proportion, reading detection confidence and the tradeoff record on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across fourteen producers rather than fourteen good crops, and the tradeoffs array is the only place an enlargement toward the interpolation cap is ever reported.
trajectory.produces: Card-ready plates with their per-frame tradeoff records.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the licensing export against the compliance note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an at-prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the plates and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: a resigned producer must not go to the counter, a photo reference points at a file nobody sent, and two producers carry different disclosure language from the other twelve. What is the agent's call and what is the mutual's to confirm is a decision, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded plates, the image map and a list of roster questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is a property of the retired printer's document rather than of the printed card, and every offset must be computed from the document's own text rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering all four copy blocks plus the photograph frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows that share a frame so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row plates bound, then render the counter cards and the compliance proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-producer single files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts the wrong face on a card.
trajectory.produces: The card run, print-resolution proofs, and per-producer files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card against the reconciled roster at trim rather than at proof scale, block by block, disclosure sentence by disclosure sentence and photograph by photograph.
trajectory.judgement: A card that is short a line and a card bound to the wrong photograph both look like success at the API boundary and both look fine on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the honest deck opener the mutual may use, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the house rendering and lay it against the portrait set.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light can live beside fourteen normalised portraits rather than the warmest thumbnail, and decide whether it joins the set or gets abandoned. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale opener, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Read the rate table and decide how three plans quoted on different bases can be presented to a family at a kitchen table without implying a comparison that is not there.
trajectory.judgement: The whole honesty of the premium infographic rests here. Presenting a rate per thousand of coverage beside a flat monthly premium as one series is the failure a non-designer ships, and it is a compliance problem as much as a design one.
trajectory.produces: A stated basis of comparison, the derived figures, and the qualification that has to travel with them.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to answer to a ninety-one year old mutual at a modest premium band, sober without being austere. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML carrying the deck roots, the one-pager at true physical dimensions, the premium infographic as inline SVG and the advisor-brand basis page, inline every photograph, set the plan comparison as a real table with its qualifying footnote under the whole table, declare family and weight per text element, then upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air a sober regulated band takes and which producer leads.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the client-facing collateral, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify the first canvas from the document's rendition and every other canvas from the returned per-canvas markup, block by block.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition shows the first artboard only, so the markup is the only channel for the rest.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the remainder.

trajectory.action: Build the compliance selects board within the placement cap, re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success. The note has to carry every roster question, every parameter applied and every producer whose photograph could not be brought to the set, before the run goes to the printer rather than after.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the fourteen separations actually holds at the edge. Five producers stood against the branch's mid-grey painted wall in a charcoal or navy suit, and where shoulder and ground sit at nearly the same value the separation bites into the shoulder or eats the collar while the call returns success and a perfectly plausible file. It is invisible at the scale an agent inspects at, because a missing sliver of a dark shoulder against a pale card ground only resolves as a chewed edge at print size. Nothing distinguishes those five frames from the other nine as thumbnails, there is no measurement anywhere in the family, and the separation itself is the diagnostic.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it: whether this producer's shoulder survives is a property of the specific photograph, and there is no read-ahead that reports edge quality. Nothing in the brief, the asset notes or any earlier step mentions the branch wall or the suits, and the acceptance line about intact shoulders is the client's standing quality bar of the same kind they already state about looking like one company. The response is not a re-run of the same operation, it is a different instrument on those frames, a selection bounded on something with contrast rather than a whole-frame separation, or a decision that a given producer must be re-photographed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the plates at print size rather than at preview scale, re-do the failing ones through a differently bounded selection or through a confined correction that does not rely on the ground being separable, re-judge those producers against the other nine as one set, and name any producer whose frame will not yield a clean plate before the run goes to the printer.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A regulated mutual sends fourteen counter cards to branch counters and shared bank desks with five producers whose shoulders and collars are visibly chewed away at the ground, which is the single most conspicuous defect a card at eye level on a counter can carry.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every disclosure actually arrives whole. The 2026 card's disclosure frame is a fixed measure sized to the sentence compliance wrote that year, and a fixed frame does not spill and does not warn: the text that does not fit is simply not rendered. Two producers on this roster are dually licensed and carry a materially longer state-specific paragraph, so their cards come back looking correct, laid out correctly, with the sentence stopping partway through. The merge reports success, the page count is right, the proof looks like a card, and the only place the truncation exists is on the rendered page at trim, read against the disclosure text the roster actually holds.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot avoid it, because whether a given producer's disclosure exceeds a frame built for a different sentence is a fact about the collision of the retired printer's 2026 frame with 2027 roster data, and neither the frame's capacity nor the disclosure lengths are announced anywhere. Nothing in the brief, the asset list or the deliverables states that any disclosure is longer than any other. The response is not a re-merge of the same template, it is a template decision: rebuild the disclosure frame's measure or its type size in the converted document, or take the two long-disclosure producers back to compliance, and either way re-derive the run.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read each rendered card's disclosure at trim against the roster cell it came from rather than trusting the proof's appearance, then rebuild the disclosure frame in the converted document so the longest paragraph on the roster fits, re-prepare the template, re-verify the placeholder inventory by round trip, re-merge and re-read every card again, and raise with compliance whether the longer paragraph may be set smaller than the standard one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A life insurer distributes printed counter cards on which a state-mandated disclosure stops mid-sentence, which is a regulatory exposure rather than a design defect, discovered by a state examiner or a complaint rather than by the mutual.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the plan comparison's qualifying footnote. The three plans are quoted on different bases, so the honest table needs one sentence that qualifies the whole table rather than any single column, and the natural way to author that is a footnote row spanning all the columns. Whether a spanned row survives as one cell carrying one continuous sentence, or is redistributed across the columns as separate cells, is not documented anywhere and is not visible from the export's success. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, the rendition only shows the first artboard, and a fragmented footnote still renders as a tidy row of text.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No amount of care settles it in advance, because the importer's handling of a spanning cell is not stated in any capability the agent can read, and both outcomes look like success. Nothing in the brief or the deliverables makes any claim about how the table imports; the acceptance line only states the client's requirement that a whole-table qualification read as one sentence. The response is a re-authoring decision rather than a re-run: move the qualification out of the table into its own text frame beneath it, or restructure the comparison so the differing basis is carried per column, both of which change the one-pager's composition.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup for the footnote row rather than accepting the export's success, and if the sentence has been split, re-author the one-pager so the qualification sits in its own full-measure text element under the table, re-check that the table's own cells and per-cell rules survived, re-run the readiness check and re-export, then re-verify the first canvas from the rendition and the rest from the markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The one page a producer puts in front of a family compares three plans quoted on different bases with the sentence that explains the difference broken into three column-width fragments, which reads as three separate footnotes and leaves the comparison materially misleading in exactly the way the compliance note forbids.

deliverables.name: Producer portrait set, fourteen frames brought to one house rendering
deliverables.spec: Fourteen self-submitted phone photographs brought to one skin rendering, one background value, one head size in frame and one crop logic, delivered at or below each source frame's dimensions with a per-producer parameter log and one line on why that producer differs from the others. Any producer who cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped near it. One set, not one portrait at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Counter card plates, one per producer on the house neutral
deliverables.spec: Fourteen separations of the producer from the office they were photographed in, set on the house neutral at the card's photograph proportion, with the shoulder line and collar intact at print size, no signage or third-party mark carried through, and no plate enlarged past its source. Delivered with the per-frame record of how each separation was achieved, since the office grounds differ and one method does not serve all fourteen.

deliverables.name: Northern district counter card run, press cards plus per-producer files and compliance proofs
deliverables.spec: One 4 by 6 card per active producer, card count equal to the reconciled roster, binding name, license line, office and the full disclosure verbatim plus that producer's own plate. Accompanied by one single-card file per producer, named to the roster and identity-verified by opening it, and by proofs rendered at true print resolution from the merged document. Produced by reverse-engineering the retired printer's press file into a live merge template, so the template and the record of how it was derived are handed back.

deliverables.name: Advisor deck, plan one-pager, premium infographic and brand basis page as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable document carrying the client-facing deck roots, the plan one-pager at true physical dimensions, the premium infographic as editable vector rather than a picture of a chart, and the advisor-brand basis page, with live text in one licensed type system, the plan comparison as a genuine table, and every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from so the marketing desk can change a rate itself.

deliverables.name: Handover note and compliance selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied to each portrait and why it differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, what the press file conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, the stated basis on which the three plans were compared and the qualification that travels with it, every roster row questioned and its resolution, and every enlargement any tool reported. why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome insurance brochure with invented people on it. IDENTITY: these are fourteen named appointed producers whose faces sit on cards at bank counters, and a regenerated face is a misrepresentation a licensed carrier cannot distribute. SPEC: the run is one 4 by 6 card per active producer binding four named fields verbatim, including a state-mandated disclosure that must appear complete, plus per-producer single files each containing the producer they claim and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the deck, the one-pager and the infographic are defined by being editable, because rates move annually and disclosure language changes when a state changes it. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this shoulder survive separation, did this disclosure arrive whole at trim, is this the producer the card says it is.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_tone, apply_adjustments global and masked, select_subject and select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, remove_background both transparent and with backgroundColor, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, upscale_factor and detection_confidence are all verified headless. The separation checkpoint rests on documented facts rather than invention: there is no measurement anywhere in the family, selection masks come back fully binary with zero intermediate values so no feather exists, and remove_background is documented as depending on a coherent subject blob, which is exactly what a same-value shoulder against a same-value wall fails to present. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, which makes the no-enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored so proofs must be rendered from the merged document, frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the agent's control, and the mapping readout's textContent is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. Image binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles is verified, with the single-record loop as the identity-guaranteed fallback. The disclosure checkpoint needs no unverified capability: a fixed-measure frame's overset behaviour is a property of the converted document, and reading it requires exactly the trim-resolution render the tool provides. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at 96 dpi, real tables with per-cell strokes, inline SVG as native editable vector, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows page one only so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; the payload is routed by uploaded URL because inlined portraits pass the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with a partial success read as partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no variable QR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no batch above 20.
